protocol.legal_basis: Not printed in this document: no Act, regulation or poisons schedule provision is named. The document describes itself as a 'Clinical Protocol' that 'forms part of the CVD Risk Reduction Program' (Queensland Community Pharmacy Chronic Conditions Management Pilot) and covers 'protocol-based/structured prescribing of medicines for the management of dyslipidaemia' (p.4). Operating conditions printed: 'When applying the information contained within this clinical protocol, pharmacists should exercise professional discretion and judgement. The protocol supports, but does not replace, the pharmacist's responsibility to make decisions appropriate to the circumstances of the individual, in consultation with the patient and/or their caregiver.' (p.3).
protocol.supervision_model: collaborative — document terminology: 'J: Collaborative care' (p.13); patients enrolled at Entry point 1 are managed 'concurrent to referral to an appropriate healthcare provider for further review and collaborative care' (p.4); 'An update must be provided to the patient's usual healthcare provider following each occasion of care' (Entry point 2, p.4); 'When modifying pharmacotherapy regimens for lipid modification that have been prescribed by another healthcare provider, attempt to notify and make changes in collaboration with the original prescriber or the patient's usual healthcare provider (whichever is most appropriate).' (p.11); 'the protocol supports, but does not replace, the pharmacist's responsibility to make decisions appropriate to the circumstances of the individual' (p.3).
protocol.scope_summary: Queensland Community Pharmacy Chronic Conditions Management Pilot clinical protocol (V2) for the CVD Risk Reduction Program: Lipid Modification. It sets eligibility/ineligibility (aged 18–79, pregnancy, complex CVD, secondary dyslipidaemia, abnormal pathology, lipid targets not reached after 6 months etc.), the A–K assessment and management pathway (eligibility, consent/enrolment, CVD risk assessment, history, measurements, test review, non-pharmacological measures, pharmacotherapy with up to two agents — statins, ezetimibe, fenofibrate — monitoring with lipid target tables, confirmation of plan, communication, collaborative care, ongoing review), referral triggers, an Appendix CVD Risk Management Plan and a reference list. It is used in conjunction with the Clinical Protocol: Hypertension and Clinical Protocol: Blood Glucose Management.

diagnosis_pathways.name: CVD Risk Reduction Program: Lipid Modification — sections A to K (assessment and management pathway)

steps.description: A: Program eligibility — 'Confirm eligibility to participate in the Program (see Eligibility).'; 'Consider program eligibility at every consultation, as eligibility can change at any time.'; 'Refer the patient to their usual healthcare provider with comprehensive clinical handover if the patient is, or becomes, ineligible for management under the Program.' Figure 1 eligibility box: 'Person aged ≥18 years and ≤79 years' and 'Confirm the patient does not meet any ineligibility criteria (refer to page 1)'. Entry points (p.4): Entry point 1 — no previous diagnosis of dyslipidaemia, no ineligibility criteria, enrol with management concurrent to referral; Entry point 2 — existing diagnosis of dyslipidaemia, no ineligibility criteria, enrol with ongoing monitoring and management and update the usual healthcare provider after each occasion of care.

gates.criterion: Patient is aged ≥18 years and ≤79 years and does not meet any ineligibility criteria (EXC-1 to EXC-29)

provenance.section_heading: A: Program eligibility

steps.description: Provide an overview of the Program including aims, expected outcomes and what the Program may involve: 'timeframes for management of the condition, such as the number of appointments and testing required, and the costs involved'; 'how the patient's medicines may be managed and how medicine costs may differ when prescribed by a pharmacist'; 'other interventions that may be recommended as part of the Program e.g., smoking cessation and weight management'; 'that the patient may leave the Program, including by opting out or becoming ineligible, at any time, and be referred to an appropriate healthcare provider.' Then 'Provide Program overview, gain consent and enrol in Program' and 'Document informed consent from the patient for participation, as per the Pilot Handbook.'

gates.criterion: Informed consent documented from the patient for participation, as per the Pilot Handbook

provenance.section_heading: Overview of the CVD Risk Reduction Program: Lipid modification

steps.description: Assess CVD risk: 'All patients entering the CVD Risk Reduction Program for Lipid Modification must have their CVD risk assessed (see Clinical Protocol: Hypertension for detail on CVD risk assessment).' 'Reassess CVD risk every 5 years for patients at low CVD risk, or every 2 years for patients at intermediate CVD risk (or sooner where there is a significant change to risk factors) (1).' 'For patients already receiving pharmacological therapy to reduce their cardiovascular risk, or who have previously been assessed as high-risk, review individual risk factors. Formal reassessment of overall CVD risk is not recommended for these patients (1).' Risk category (High / Intermediate / Low / Severe hyperlipidaemia) drives the Table 1 approach to lipid modification (p.10).

gates.criterion: CVD risk assessed before/when entering the Program (detail in the Clinical Protocol: Hypertension)

provenance.section_heading: Figure 1: Overview of the CVD Risk Reduction Program: lipid modification

steps.description: B: Patient history — 'Obtain sufficient information to assess the patient's condition, and the safety and appropriateness of any recommendations and medicines for the patient.' Consider: age; ethnic or cultural background, including Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status; lactation status; previous and current medical conditions; clinical signs of undiagnosed familial hypercholesterolaemia (e.g., tendon xanthomata, corneal arcus before 45 years of age, xanthelasma); alarm signs and symptoms that require further investigation (e.g., unexplained weight loss or gain, frequent headache and dizziness, chronic nausea and vomiting); family history of CVD, including familial hypercholesterolaemia; smoking status and history (tobacco, cannabis, vaping, passive smoking or other exposure); all current and recently ceased treatments; drug and non-drug allergies and adverse drug reactions; recent pathology results, including lipid profile, liver and thyroid function tests; diet/nutrition status and weight; levels of physical activity; recreational or illicit drug use, and alcohol use; specialist involvement in care. Reminder: 'Pharmacists can access a range of clinical information in a patient's My Health Record...'

gates.criterion: No alarm signs and symptoms that require further investigation are identified (e.g., unexplained weight loss or gain, frequent headache and dizziness, chronic nausea and vomiting) and no clinical signs of undiagnosed familial hypercholesterolaemia are present

provenance.section_heading: B: Patient history

steps.description: C: Take measurements — 1) BP: 'Conduct BP measurements in accordance with the National Heart Foundation of Australia Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of hypertension in adults 2016 (5).' 'Take three measurements and average the last two. Where there is variation >10 mmHg systolic or >6 mmHg diastolic, have the patient rest quietly for 5 minutes then remeasure.' 2) Weight and height: measure to calculate BMI (Heart Foundation BMI calculator (6); Department of Health and Aging - BMI and waist measurement (7) for BMI ranges and exceptions). 3) Waist circumference: measure waist (Heart Foundation resource (8)) and interpret per Department of Health and Aging - BMI and waist measurement (7).

gates.criterion: BP readings are within ≤10 mmHg systolic and ≤6 mmHg diastolic variation (on fail: have the patient rest quietly for 5 minutes then remeasure)

provenance.section_heading: C: Take measurements

steps.description: D: Review test results — 'Where recent test results are unavailable, undertake appropriate testing (point of care testing (PoCT) and/or laboratory testing). Refer to the Pilot Handbook for further information regarding options for requesting laboratory testing.' Lipid profile: 'Patients with abnormal lipid levels identified during CVD risk assessment should have a repeat fasting lipid profile conducted on another day to confirm the result and inform management (9).' Other testing: 'Consider if any other PoCT or laboratory testing (e.g., liver function, renal function, full blood count, creatine kinase) is needed to inform patient management.'

gates.criterion: Abnormal lipid levels identified during CVD risk assessment are confirmed by a repeat fasting lipid profile conducted on another day before management is informed

provenance.section_heading: D: Review test results

steps.description: E: Non-pharmacological measures — 'Provide all patients with information about non-pharmacological measures, regardless of whether pharmacotherapy is prescribed.' 'The 5As Framework for behavioural risk modification may be used ... in accordance with the ... SNAP guide (10).' 'Lifestyle modification (e.g. dietary changes, physical activity) can improve lipid concentrations (2).' Smoking and vaping cessation (guidelines (11), (12)); Weight management ('Lipid concentrations are shown to improve with weight loss in patients who are overweight or obese (2)'). Diet and nutrition: patients with dyslipidaemia should (2, 15) '• reduce saturated and trans-fat intake by replacing them with mono and poly-unsaturated fats (avocado, nuts, seeds and vegetable oils) • increase fibre intake (particularly soluble fibre e.g., oats, psyllium and legumes) • use products enriched with plant sterols • include soy protein in their diet through soy milk and/or soy cheese • aim for 2-3 servings of oily fish per week (salmon, mackerel and tuna).' 'Encourage all patients with an intermediate or high CVD risk to see a dietitian for individualised nutritional advice.' Physical activity: in line with Physical activity and exercise guidelines for all Australians (16); 'Referral to an exercise physiologist and/or physiotherapist to develop an exercise plan may be required.' Alcohol consumption: 'Alcohol consumption has a mixed effect on lipid profile.'

provenance.section_heading: E: Non-pharmacological measures

steps.description: F: Pharmacotherapy — 'Pharmacists may prescribe up to two agents (dual-therapy) from the following list in line with the current online version of Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular (Lipid modification) (2): • statins (first line therapy unless contraindicated or not tolerated). Initiate high dose of a high potency statin if the patient has a high CVD risk or LDL-C levels are >4.0 mmol/L • ezetimibe (may be used as monotherapy if statins are contraindicated or not tolerated) • fenofibrate (may be used as additional therapy to meet triglyceride targets).' 'Combination products can be prescribed if appropriate, however they must only include medicines able to be prescribed under the Program.' Table 1 approach: High CVD risk — 'Pharmacotherapy is recommended for all patients in addition to lifestyle modification'; Intermediate CVD risk — 'Consider lipid modifying pharmacotherapy depending on the clinical context; A trial of lifestyle modification may be sufficient to manage CVD risk; Discuss the potential benefits and harms of treatment with the patient and encourage shared decision-making.'; Low CVD risk — 'Pharmacotherapy is not routinely recommended; If dyslipidaemia is present, discuss lifestyle modification. Lipid-modifying pharmacotherapy can be considered in those who do not reach the LDL-C target with lifestyle support'; Severe hyperlipidaemia (serum total cholesterol ≥7.5 mmol/L or LDL cholesterol ≥5 mmol/L) — 'Manage regardless of AusCVDRisk calculator results. Refer these patients to their usual healthcare provider for management.'; Abnormal lipid levels (but not severe hyperlipidaemia) in patients who cannot have their CVD risk calculated — 'Refer these patients to their usual healthcare provider for review and possible management.' Before initiating/modifying consider age, liver function, CVD risk, current lipid profile, related comorbidities, clinical targets, contraindications/adverse reactions/drug interactions, response to previous interventions and patient preference (including cost). Prescriptions (including repeats) 'should provide enough medicine for the period until the patient's next scheduled review.' Pharmacists may modify/adjust existing lipid modification pharmacotherapy if 'patient's response is inadequate (within appropriate clinical timeframes)' or 'patient is experiencing intolerable or unmanageable adverse effects'; when modifying regimens prescribed by another healthcare provider, 'attempt to notify and make changes in collaboration with the original prescriber or the patient's usual healthcare provider (whichever is most appropriate).'

gates.criterion: No more than two agents (dual-therapy) are prescribed from the permitted list (statins, ezetimibe, fenofibrate), and any combination product only includes medicines able to be prescribed under the Program

provenance.section_heading: Pharmacotherapy treatment options under the Program

steps.description: G: Monitoring and clinical targets — 'Monitor response to new or changed pharmacotherapy by measuring lipid concentrations after 6 weeks (see Table 3 for target levels) (2).' 'If already prescribed a statin but not reaching clinical targets (2): • review adherence and address any issues • consider increasing the dose of the statin (if not already at maximum dose) or switching to a high potency statin • consider adding a second medicine and modify the dose to optimise management: – ezetimibe (if LDL-C targets are not being met) – fenofibrate (if triglyceride targets are not being met on a combination of statin and fish oil).' 'If clinical targets have not been reached 6 months after commencing lipid modifying therapy, refer the patient to an appropriate healthcare provider for ongoing management. If clinical targets have been reached after 6 months in the Program, continue to monitor response to therapy.' Table 2 (tests/monitoring per drug class) and Table 3 (target levels of cholesterol) apply.

gates.criterion: Lipid concentrations measured 6 weeks after new or changed pharmacotherapy show response to therapy and the medicine is tolerated
Clinical targets reached (and stable) after 6 months of lipid modifying therapy

provenance.section_heading: G: Monitoring and clinical targets

steps.description: H: Confirm management plan is appropriate — 'Consult the Therapeutic Guidelines (2), the Australian Medicines Handbook (19) and other relevant resources to confirm that management is appropriate, including: contraindications and precautions; drug and disease interactions; lactation status.'

gates.criterion: Contraindications and precautions, drug and disease interactions, and lactation status confirmed appropriate against Therapeutic Guidelines, the Australian Medicines Handbook and other relevant resources

provenance.section_heading: H: Confirm management plan is appropriate

steps.description: I: Communicate agreed management plan — 'Provide comprehensive advice (including supporting written information) to the patient regarding: individual product and medicine use; non-pharmacological measures; how to manage adverse effects; when to seek further care and/or treatment; when to return for clinical review.' 'Document the agreed management plan and individualised clinical targets within the patient's CVD Risk Management Plan.' 'It is the pharmacist's responsibility to ensure the suitability and accuracy of any resources provided to patients (and caregivers if applicable) and that they comply with all copyright conditions.'

provenance.section_heading: I: Communicate agreed management plan

steps.description: J: Collaborative care — 'Provide a copy of the patient's CVD Risk Management Plan to the patient's usual healthcare provider (and any other relevant health professionals involved in the patient's care). The communication should also include (if relevant): relevant medical history and pathology/PoCT results; changes to existing pharmacotherapy or new pharmacotherapy prescribed; a summary of advice provided to the patient including recommendations for multidisciplinary care and referrals; the next scheduled review appointment.'

provenance.section_heading: J: Collaborative care

steps.description: K: Clinical review and ongoing collaboration — 'All patients should undergo regular clinical review to participate in the Program. Review patients 6 weeks after initiating or modifying the treatment regimen or sooner, if required or as recommended (2).' 'Prior to each periodic review, arrange any relevant laboratory tests (that are not performed by PoCT) required for monitoring.' At each appointment review: ongoing eligibility; patient history; BP measurements; pathology or PoCT; changes to CVD risk factors; response to current management and adherence to lifestyle modification; prescribed pharmacotherapy; CVD Risk Management Plan and clinical targets. 'Provide an update to the patient's usual healthcare provider following each occasion of care including when any changes are made to the patient's management plan.' 'Patients are not eligible for participation in the Program if their clinical targets have not been reached after 6 months of lipid modifying therapy.' 'Refer all patients (with their consent) who are no longer eligible for management within the Program, or who do not wish to continue in the Program, to an appropriate healthcare provider.'

gates.criterion: Patient's condition remains eligible to be managed in the Program, they wish to remain in the Program and continue to consent, and they attend scheduled reviews

provenance.section_heading: K: Clinical review and ongoing collaboration

treatments.notes: No specific statin, dose, strength, route, frequency or quantity is printed in this protocol; prescribing must follow 'the current online version of Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular (Lipid modification) (2)'. 'statins (first line therapy unless contraindicated or not tolerated). Initiate high dose of a high potency statin if the patient has a high CVD risk or LDL-C levels are >4.0 mmol/L'. Escalation when not at target (p.11-12): 'review adherence and address any issues'; 'consider increasing the dose of the statin (if not already at maximum dose) or switching to a high potency statin'; 'consider adding a second medicine ... ezetimibe (if LDL-C targets are not being met) – fenofibrate (if triglyceride targets are not being met on a combination of statin and fish oil).' Monitoring (Table 2, p.12): 'Blood tests for baseline liver function and creatine kinase (CK) should be taken before initiating and re-tested if clinically indicated.' Pregnancy/lactation/paediatric caveats (verbatim): patients who 'are planning a pregnancy or are pregnant' and those 'aged <18 years or >79 years' are ineligible for the Program (p.1); 'lactation status' must be considered in patient history (p.7) and confirmed under 'H: Confirm management plan is appropriate — ... lactation status' (p.12). Prescriptions (including repeats) 'should provide enough medicine for the period until the patient's next scheduled review' (p.10).

provenance.section_heading: Pharmacotherapy treatment options under the Program

treatments.notes: No dose, strength, route, frequency or quantity is printed; follow the current online Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular (Lipid modification). 'ezetimibe (may be used as monotherapy if statins are contraindicated or not tolerated)'. Add-on use: 'consider adding a second medicine ... ezetimibe (if LDL-C targets are not being met)' (p.12). One of the agents pharmacists may prescribe (up to two agents/dual-therapy). Pregnancy/lactation/paediatric caveats (verbatim): 'are planning a pregnancy or are pregnant' and 'aged <18 years or >79 years' are ineligible (p.1); 'lactation status' considered in history (p.7) and confirmed at plan check (p.12).

provenance.section_heading: Pharmacotherapy treatment options under the Program

'fenofibrate (may be used as additional therapy to meet triglyceride targets).' Add-on use: 'consider adding a second medicine ... fenofibrate (if triglyceride targets are not being met on a combination of statin and fish oil)' (p.12). Monitoring (Table 2, p.12): 'Blood tests for full blood count and liver function should be taken before initiating and at 3 monthly intervals during the first year of treatment.' 'HDL - paradoxical decrease in HDL concentration has occurred weeks to years after starting fenofibrate; consider stopping fenofibrate if HDL is markedly decreased from baseline.' Pregnancy/lactation/paediatric caveats (verbatim): 'are planning a pregnancy or are pregnant' and 'aged <18 years or >79 years' are ineligible (p.1); 'lactation status' considered in history (p.7) and confirmed at plan check (p.12).

open_questions.observed: The document names no Act, regulation or poisons schedule provision; it only describes itself as a 'Clinical Protocol' of the Queensland Community Pharmacy Chronic Conditions Management Pilot covering 'protocol-based/structured prescribing of medicines for the management of dyslipidaemia' (p.4) with pharmacists to 'exercise professional discretion and judgement' (p.3).
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec requires legal_basis naming the regulation/schedule provision; nothing printed to transcribe, so it is recorded as not printed rather than inferred.

open_questions.topic: No doses, strengths, quantities or schedules printed for lipid-modifying agents
open_questions.observed: F: Pharmacotherapy lists agents only (statins — 'Initiate high dose of a high potency statin if the patient has a high CVD risk or LDL-C levels are >4.0 mmol/L', ezetimibe, fenofibrate) and defers to 'the current online version of Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular (Lipid modification) (2)'. Table 2 gives testing requirements only.
open_questions.why_unclear: Dosing fields (form, strength, dose, route, frequency, duration, max_quantity, quantity_to_supply) are left blank because no numeric dosing is printed; the specific statin and what counts as a 'high potency' statin are not named.

open_questions.topic: Severe hyperlipidaemia: 'manage regardless and refer' (Table 1) vs ineligibility list
open_questions.observed: Table 1 (p.10) says for 'Severe hyperlipidaemia (serum total cholesterol ≥7.5 mmol/L or LDL cholesterol ≥5 mmol/L)': 'Manage regardless of AusCVDRisk calculator results. • Refer these patients to their usual healthcare provider for management.' The ineligibility list (p.2) says patients with 'total cholesterol ≥7.5 mmol/L, LDL-C ≥5.0 mmol/L' are ineligible for the Program (which itself triggers referral with comprehensive clinical handover).
open_questions.why_unclear: The two statements are not obviously reconcilable (ineligible-and-refer vs manage-regardless-and-refer); both readings recorded without resolution.

open_questions.observed: 'Pharmacists may modify or adjust existing lipid modification pharmacotherapy, including if the: • patient's response is inadequate (within appropriate clinical timeframes)' (p.11).
open_questions.why_unclear: No numeric timeframe is printed; the only fixed interval in the protocol is the 6-month target rule (p.12). Recorded as printed and flagged for local policy.

open_questions.topic: Table 1 approach rows split across pages 10-11
open_questions.observed: The 'Severe hyperlipidaemia' row begins on page 10 and continues on page 11, and the 'Abnormal lipid levels (but not severe hyperlipidaemia) in patients who cannot have their CVD risk calculated' row sits entirely on page 11; column alignment in the extraction is approximate.
open_questions.why_unclear: Table row/column boundaries cannot be read with certainty from the extraction; rows transcribed best-effort and flagged for verification against the PDF.

open_questions.topic: 'urinary albumin creatinine ratio' hyphen lost in extraction
open_questions.observed: Page 1 extracts as 'persistent albuminuria: urinary albumin / creatinine ratio (uACR) ≥3 mg/mmol' split across a line break; the companion Blood Glucose Management protocol prints 'urinary albumin-creatinine ratio (uACR)'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Hyphenation cannot be confirmed from this extraction; transcribed as extracted with confidence 'medium' and both readings noted.

open_questions.observed: Referral destinations and criteria appear from page 1 (eligibility) through page 14 (ongoing eligibility), plus appendix referral prompts on page 16.
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec allows one shared provenance object for the referral block; first page (1) used and the range recorded here.

open_questions.topic: Pathway gates where the document states no consequence
open_questions.observed: Three gates are recorded with on_fail 'unclear': (a) 'All patients entering ... must have their CVD risk assessed' (p.5); (b) 'alarm signs and symptoms that require further investigation' / signs of undiagnosed familial hypercholesterolaemia (p.7); (c) confirming management is appropriate incl. lactation status (p.12).
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not say what happens when these requirements are not met (refer? stop? recheck?), so no on_fail was inferred.

open_questions.observed: Document footer/title states 'Clinical Protocol – V2'; the version table on page 18 shows 'Version 2.0 | 07.04.2026 | Updates across sections to reflect contemporary guidance and improve usability.' No separate 'effective date' line is printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: effective_date taken from the version-history date for Version 2.0; confirm it is the operative date rather than a publication date.

open_questions.observed: The document requires updates/copies to the patient's usual healthcare provider but says nothing about notifiable conditions or statutory notifications; My Health Record is mentioned only as an information source (p.7).
open_questions.why_unclear: notifiable.required is set true only for the printed healthcare-provider notification duties; silence on statutory notification recorded here.

open_questions.observed: No non-emergency 'urgent' referral wording is printed; the only escalation above routine is '(or emergency services, if required)' (p.1) and the Appendix entry 'Closest 24-hour emergency services' (p.17).
open_questions.why_unclear: referral.urgent is empty because the document genuinely prints no urgent-tier destination; recorded rather than inferred.

open_questions.observed: CVD Risk Management Plan prints 'Total cholesterol: Less than 5.5/ 4.0 mmol/L' — two values separated by a slash with no explanation (p.15).
open_questions.why_unclear: Ambiguous as printed (possibly two alternative targets or a stray character); transcribed verbatim without interpretation.

open_questions.topic: Fish oil referenced but not a prescribable agent
open_questions.observed: The escalation rule mentions 'fenofibrate (if triglyceride targets are not being met on a combination of statin and fish oil)' (p.12), but fish oil is not listed among the agents pharmacists may prescribe under the Program (statins, ezetimibe, fenofibrate).
open_questions.why_unclear: Status of fish oil (who supplies it, at what dose) is not defined in the document; captured as a non-supply treatment row with empty dosing fields.

open_questions.topic: Clinical signs of undiagnosed familial hypercholesterolaemia — no stated action
open_questions.observed: 'Consider: ... clinical signs of undiagnosed familial hypercholesterolaemia (e.g., tendon xanthomata, corneal arcus before 45 years of age, xanthelasma)' (p.7), while an existing diagnosis of familial hypercholesterolaemia is an ineligibility criterion (p.1).
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not state what to do when these signs are found (recheck eligibility? refer? test?); captured in the pathway history step with gate on_fail 'unclear'.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Legal basis of the protocol (which Queensland regulation/poisons schedule provision the pilot operates under).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document prints no Act or regulation; must be confirmed with Queensland Health before go-live (spec rule 7).

hugh_to_confirm.item: Which statin, at what dose/potency, and the meaning of 'high dose of a high potency statin' (initiate when 'high CVD risk or LDL-C levels are >4.0 mmol/L'), plus doses for ezetimibe and fenofibrate.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: No dosing is printed; the protocol defers to 'the current online version of Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular (Lipid modification)'. Local formulary/dosing data must be sourced and verified before the rules engine can prescribe.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Pharmacists may prescribe up to two agents (dual-therapy)' and 'Combination products can be prescribed if appropriate, however they must only include medicines able to be prescribed under the Program.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The two-agent cap and the set of permitted combination products must be encoded as a local hard rule; the permitted product list is not printed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'patient's response is inadequate (within appropriate clinical timeframes)' as the trigger to modify existing lipid modification pharmacotherapy.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Undefined timeframe; local policy must set the numeric timeframe (distinct from the printed 6-month target rule).

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'When applying the information contained within this clinical protocol, pharmacists should exercise professional discretion and judgement. The protocol supports, but does not replace, the pharmacist's responsibility to make decisions appropriate to the circumstances of the individual...'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Open-ended professional judgement clause needs a defined boundary before an automated rules engine can rely on it.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Referral destinations expressed as 'their usual healthcare provider', 'an appropriate healthcare provider' and 'emergency services, if required'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Destinations are undefined; local policy must map each trigger to an approved destination/urgency.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Conflicting handling of severe hyperlipidaemia: Table 1 'Manage regardless of AusCVDRisk calculator results. • Refer these patients to their usual healthcare provider for management.' vs ineligibility criterion 'total cholesterol ≥7.5 mmol/L, LDL-C ≥5.0 mmol/L'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Operational handling (enrol-and-manage vs screen-out-and-refer) must be resolved with Queensland Health before go-live; both readings recorded in open_questions.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Document informed consent from the patient for participation, as per the Pilot Handbook.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Consent process lives in an external document (Pilot Handbook); confirm the local consent wording/record before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Where recent test results are unavailable, undertake appropriate testing (point of care testing (PoCT) and/or laboratory testing). Refer to the Pilot Handbook for further information regarding options for requesting laboratory testing.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: PoCT/laboratory request arrangements are delegated to the Pilot Handbook; local ordering pathways and pathology request forms must be confirmed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Written referral exception to specialist-treatment ineligibility: 'unless they have a written referral from their treating specialist or general practitioner to participate in the Program'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Local process for verifying/holding the written referral (e.g. copy on file, My Health Record) must be confirmed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Table 2 monitoring schedule (statin baseline liver function and CK; fenofibrate FBC and liver function before initiating and 3-monthly in the first year, serum CK, renal function dose reduction if CrCl is 30–60 mL/minute, HDL stop-review).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Monitoring intervals and the CrCl-based dose-reduction rule must be configured as schedulable checks in the local system and aligned with local pathology ordering.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Individualised lipid targets (Table 3 risk-category targets vs Appendix plan targets 'individualise as required') and shared decision-making: 'Patients should be involved in shared decision-making and the development of their CVD Risk Management Plan, including setting of appropriate targets.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Two target sets are printed and the appendix targets are marked 'individualise as required'; local defaults and the allowed target range must be confirmed before automated target checks.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'When modifying pharmacotherapy regimens for lipid modification that have been prescribed by another healthcare provider, attempt to notify and make changes in collaboration with the original prescriber or the patient's usual healthcare provider (whichever is most appropriate).'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: 'Attempt to notify' and 'whichever is most appropriate' leave the collaboration workflow to local policy; define the notification method and fallback.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Fish oil use: 'fenofibrate (if triglyceride targets are not being met on a combination of statin and fish oil)' — fish oil is referenced but not listed as a prescribable agent under the Program.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Local policy must state whether fish oil can be supplied/prescribed under the Program or is expected to be patient-purchased/already prescribed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Intermediate CVD risk option: 'Consider lipid modifying pharmacotherapy depending on the clinical context • A trial of lifestyle modification may be sufficient ... • Discuss the potential benefits and harms of treatment with the patient and encourage shared decision-making.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Clinician-judgement branch with no decision rule printed; local policy must define how the decision is recorded and when pharmacotherapy is started.
